title: Locally constant maps form a sheaf of sets
statement: Let U be a topological space and R a set. A map from an open subset V of U to R is locally constant if every point of V has an open neighbourhood in V on which the map is constant. For each open V let L_R(V) be the set of such maps, with restriction maps. Then L_R is a sheaf of sets on the site of open subsets of U with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: compatible locally constant maps on an open cover glue uniquely to a locally constant map.

source.place: Sheaves, Example 6.4 and Definition 6.5 (Tag 006W): continuous maps form a sheaf; for a discrete target these are the locally constant maps

proof.text: Let $V=\bigcup_{i\in I}V_i$ be an open covering and let $f_i:V_i\to R$ be locally constant maps whose restrictions to every $V_i\cap V_j$ agree. Define $f:V\to R$ pointwise by $f(x)=f_i(x)$ for any $i$ with $x\in V_i$. Such an $i$ exists because the $V_i$ cover $V$, and compatibility on $V_i\cap V_j$ makes the value independent of the choice. By construction $f|_{V_i}=f_i$ for every $i$.

For $x\in V$, choose $i$ with $x\in V_i$. Since $f_i$ is locally constant, there is an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq V_i$ of $x$ on which $f_i$ is constant; because $V_i$ is open in $V$, $W$ is also open in $V$, and $f|_W=f_i|_W$ is constant. Thus $f$ is locally constant. If $g:V\to R$ is another gluing, then for each $x$ and any $i$ containing it, $g(x)=f_i(x)=f(x)$, so $g=f$. Existence and uniqueness give the sheaf condition.
